options: люстра
люстры
люстре
люстрой
cases.explain: Люстра is the subject of the intransitive verb горит (is burning/lit), so it takes the nominative case.

options: зала
залы
зале
залой
cases.explain: The preposition от (from) always governs the genitive case: залы.

options: часы
часов
часам
часами
cases.explain: The preposition к (by/toward) with a time expression governs the dative case: часам.

options: карта
карты
карте
карту
cases.explain: Задумать (to think of/pick) is transitive; its direct object takes the accusative case: карту.

cases.sentence: Чтобы он купил на ее имя с ___ долга.
options: перевод
перевода
переводу
переводом
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) expressing accompaniment governs the instrumental case: переводом.

cases.sentence: То на ___ играешь и кий сломал.
options: бильярд
бильярда
бильярду
бильярде
cases.explain: The preposition на (at/on) combined with an activity takes the prepositional case: бильярде.

reading.ru: Слышно, как в передней играет еврейский оркестр, тот самый, о котором упоминается во втором акте.
reading.question: What is happening in the front hall as Act Three begins?
options: A Jewish orchestra, the same one mentioned in Act Two, is playing
A fire has broken out
The auction is being held there
Firs is serving dinner
reading.correct: A Jewish orchestra, the same one mentioned in Act Two, is playing
reading.explain: The stage direction notes that the same Jewish orchestra mentioned in Act Two is playing in the front hall.

reading.ru: Варя тихо плачет и, танцуя, утирает слезы.
reading.question: What is Varya doing while dancing at the ball?
options: Quietly crying and wiping away tears
Laughing loudly with Lopakhin
Refusing to dance at all
Arguing with the musicians
reading.correct: Quietly crying and wiping away tears
reading.explain: The stage direction shows Varya quietly crying and wiping her tears even as she dances.

reading.ru: Пищик, я полнокровный, со мной уже два раза удар был, танцевать трудно
reading.question: What health complaint does Pishchik mention to explain why dancing is hard for him?
options: He is full-blooded and has already had two strokes
He has a broken leg
He is too old to stand
He has a fever
reading.correct: He is full-blooded and has already had two strokes
reading.explain: Pishchik says he is full-blooded and has already suffered two strokes, making dancing difficult.

reading.ru: Мой покойный родитель, шутник, царство небесное, насчет нашего происхождения говорил так, будто древний род наш Симеоновых пищиков происходит будто бы от той самой лошади, которую Каллигула посадил в Сенате.
reading.question: What comic claim does Pishchik make about his family's ancestry?
options: That his family descends from the horse Caligula seated in the Senate
That his family descends from Russian nobility
That his family descends from a famous general
That his family has royal blood from France
reading.correct: That his family descends from the horse Caligula seated in the Senate
reading.explain: Pishchik jokes that his father used to claim their family descended from the very horse that Caligula made a senator.

reading.ru: Вот наняли музыкантов, а чем платить?
reading.question: What practical worry does Varya voice about the ball?
options: That they hired musicians but have no way to pay them
That no guests showed up
That the musicians refused to play
That the ballroom is too small
reading.correct: That they hired musicians but have no way to pay them
reading.explain: Varya worries aloud that they've hired musicians for the ball but have nothing to pay them with.

reading.ru: Послезавтра триста десять рублей платить.
reading.question: What debt deadline is Pishchik anxious about?
options: He must pay 310 rubles the day after tomorrow
He must pay his rent by morning
He owes Lopakhin a large sum immediately
He must repay Gaev within the week
reading.correct: He must pay 310 rubles the day after tomorrow
reading.explain: Pishchik frets that he must pay three hundred ten rubles the day after tomorrow.

reading.ru: Торги не состоялись, по всей вероятности.
reading.question: What does Trofimov speculate about the auction, given Gaev's long absence?
options: That the auction probably didn't take place
That the auction was postponed by a week
That Lopakhin definitely won the auction
That the estate was given away for free
reading.correct: That the auction probably didn't take place
reading.explain: Trofimov speculates that, in all likelihood, the auction did not take place, since Gaev is taking so long in town.

reading.ru: Дядечка купил, я в этом уверена
reading.question: What does Varya try to reassure her mother about regarding the auction?
options: That her uncle Gaev bought the estate — she's sure of it
That the estate was never actually for sale
That Lopakhin promised not to bid
That the bank canceled the auction
reading.correct: That her uncle Gaev bought the estate — she's sure of it
reading.explain: Varya tries to reassure Lyubov Andreevna that dear uncle Gaev has bought the estate, saying she is sure of it.

reading.ru: Ярославская бабушка прислала пятнадцать тысяч, чтобы купить имение на ее имя.
reading.question: How much money did the Yaroslavl grandmother send, and for what purpose?
options: Fifteen thousand, to buy the estate in her own name
Fifty thousand, as a wedding gift for Varya
Fifteen thousand, to pay off Pishchik's debt
Five thousand, to hire more servants
reading.correct: Fifteen thousand, to buy the estate in her own name
reading.explain: Lyubov Andreevna explains the grandmother sent fifteen thousand rubles so the estate could be bought in her name.

reading.ru: Сегодня судьба моя решается.
reading.question: How does Lyubov Andreevna describe the significance of that day?
options: Her fate is being decided today
It is her birthday
It is the anniversary of her son's death
It is the day she must leave for Paris
reading.correct: Her fate is being decided today
reading.explain: Lyubov Andreevna says that her fate is being decided this very day, referring to the auction.

reading.ru: Мамочка, не могу же я сама делать ему предложение.
reading.question: What does Varya say she cannot do regarding Lopakhin?
options: Propose to him herself
Refuse to see him again
Ask him for money
Tell him she loves someone else
reading.correct: Propose to him herself
reading.explain: Varya tells her mother she cannot possibly propose to Lopakhin herself; she can only wait.

reading.ru: Хоть бы сто рублей, бросила бы я все, ушла бы подальше.
reading.question: What does Varya say she would do if she had even a hundred rubles?
options: Drop everything and go far away, perhaps to a monastery
Buy new clothes for the ball
Pay off Pishchik's debt
Give it to Lopakhin as a gift
reading.correct: Drop everything and go far away, perhaps to a monastery
reading.explain: Varya says that with even a hundred rubles she would abandon everything and go far away, perhaps into a monastery.

reading.ru: Епиходов бильярдный кий сломал.
reading.question: What mishap does Yasha report about Yepikhodov?
options: He broke the billiard cue
He fell down the stairs
He lost the ball's key
He set fire to the curtains
reading.correct: He broke the billiard cue
reading.explain: Yasha reports, barely holding back laughter, that Yepikhodov broke the billiard cue.

reading.ru: Ведь я родилась здесь.
reading.question: Why does Lyubov Andreevna say she cannot imagine life without the estate?
options: Because she was born here
Because she inherited it from her husband
Because it is the only property she owns
Because her children were born here
reading.correct: Because she was born here
reading.explain: Lyubov Andreevna pleads that she was born here, and her father, mother, and grandfather lived here too.

reading.ru: Без вишневого сада я не понимаю своей жизни.
reading.question: What does Lyubov Andreevna say about her life and the cherry orchard?
options: That she cannot understand her life without the cherry orchard
That she never really loved the orchard
That the orchard means nothing to her now
That she is happy to be rid of the orchard
reading.correct: That she cannot understand her life without the cherry orchard
reading.explain: She declares that without the cherry orchard she does not understand her own life.

reading.ru: Ведь мой сын утонул здесь, плачет.
reading.question: What painful memory does Lyubov Andreevna bring up while embracing Trofimov?
options: That her son drowned here
That her husband proposed to her here
That she first met Trofimov here
That her mother died in this room
reading.correct: That her son drowned here
reading.explain: While embracing Trofimov, she cries that her son drowned right there, tying her grief to the estate.

reading.ru: Это из Парижа телеграмма.
reading.question: Where is the telegram Trofimov picks up from the floor from?
options: Paris
Yaroslavl
Kharkov
Moscow
reading.correct: Paris
reading.explain: Trofimov picks up the fallen telegram and notes it is from Paris.

reading.ru: Он мелкий негодяй, ничтожество
reading.question: How does Trofimov describe the man in Paris who has been mistreating Lyubov Andreevna?
options: A petty scoundrel, a nonentity
A brilliant but cruel businessman
A kind man who made mistakes
A wealthy nobleman
reading.correct: A petty scoundrel, a nonentity
reading.explain: Trofimov bluntly calls the man a petty scoundrel and a nonentity, saying only she doesn't see it.

reading.ru: Вам двадцать шесть лет или двадцать семь, а вы все еще гимназист второго класса
reading.question: How does Lyubov Andreevna mock Trofimov's maturity?
options: She says he's 26 or 27 yet still acts like a second-year schoolboy
She says he's too old to still be a student
She says he dresses like a child
She says he can't hold a job
reading.correct: She says he's 26 or 27 yet still acts like a second-year schoolboy
reading.explain: Angered, she tells him that at twenty-six or twenty-seven he is still like a second-form schoolboy.

reading.ru: Петя с лестницы упал.
reading.question: What comic mishap does Anya report, running in laughing?
options: Petya fell down the stairs
Petya broke a vase
Petya fainted on the dance floor
Petya lost his glasses
reading.correct: Petya fell down the stairs
reading.explain: Anya runs in laughing to report that Petya fell down the stairs.

reading.ru: Прежде у нас на балах танцевали генералы, бароны, адмиралы.
reading.question: What does Firs say about the guests at balls in the old days?
options: Generals, barons, and admirals used to dance at their balls
Only family members were invited
No one ever danced, only listened to music
Peasants were the main guests
reading.correct: Generals, barons, and admirals used to dance at their balls
reading.explain: Firs recalls that in the old days generals, barons, and admirals used to dance at their balls, unlike the postal clerk and stationmaster now invited.

reading.ru: А сейчас на кухне какой-то человек говорил, что вишневый сад уже продан сегодня
reading.question: What rumor does Anya report hearing in the kitchen?
options: That the cherry orchard has already been sold today
That Lopakhin has left for Kharkov
That the musicians have been paid
That Gaev has won money at the bank
reading.correct: That the cherry orchard has already been sold today
reading.explain: Anya reports overhearing someone in the kitchen say that the cherry orchard has already been sold that day.

reading.ru: Продан вишневый сад?
reading.question: What urgent question does Lyubov Andreevna ask Lopakhin when he finally returns?
options: Whether the cherry orchard has been sold
Whether Gaev is safe
Whether the musicians can be paid
Whether the telegram has arrived
reading.correct: Whether the cherry orchard has been sold
reading.explain: As soon as Lopakhin returns, Lyubov Andreevna anxiously asks whether the cherry orchard has been sold.

reading.ru: Вишневый сад теперь мой, мой!
reading.question: How does Lopakhin exult after revealing he bought the estate?
options: He shouts that the cherry orchard is now his, his!
He apologizes for buying it
He offers to sell it back immediately
He insists Gaev keep the deed
reading.correct: He shouts that the cherry orchard is now his, his!
reading.explain: Lopakhin laughs and exults that the cherry orchard is now his, repeating 'mine, mine.'

reading.ru: Мы насадим новый сад, роскошнее этого.
reading.question: What does Anya promise her weeping mother at the very end of the act?
options: That they will plant a new orchard, more splendid than this one
That she will buy back the old orchard someday
That Lopakhin will let them stay in the house
That Gaev will find a new source of income
reading.correct: That they will plant a new orchard, more splendid than this one
reading.explain: Anya comforts her mother, promising they will plant a new garden, more luxurious than this one.
